pool.text: Islets in the bay were known as les îlets du Prince.
A captain named de Saint-André sailed into the bay in Le Prince.
A new city was built and incorporated as Port-au-Prince.
Port-au-Prince replaced Cap-Français as the capital of the colony of Saint-Domingue.
French commissioner Étienne Polverel renamed the city to Port-Républicain.
British troops captured the city after the Battle of Port-Républicain.
Port-au-Prince became the capital of newly independent Haiti.
The city was re-established as the capital of all of unified Haiti.
The National Palace was destroyed and then rebuilt.
The National Museum was established in the palace grounds.
Toussaint Louverture International Airport opened north of the city.
A massive earthquake catastrophically affected Port-au-Prince.
An estimated thirteen thousand tap-taps were in active use.
Hurricane Sandy brought deaths, damage, and a resurgence of cholera.
The construction of a new LDS Temple was announced.
Hurricane Matthew caused catastrophic damage and hundreds of deaths.
Extensive gang violence began to paralyze Port-au-Prince.
The population of the city was estimated at one million two hundred thousand.
City Hall employees protested against a lack of salaries.
A popular tourist hub fell victim to arson.
